newsitem.title: USA: Bath Iron Works unveils $307 mln expansion plan.
newsitem.headline: Bath Iron Works unveils $307 mln expansion plan.

text.p: The Bath Iron Works unit of General Dynamics Corp has unveiled a $307 million proposal to modernize and expand its shipbuilding facility here.
The defense contractor told local officials Tuesday night that the project is needed to keep the company competitive.
It also said the project could lead to the closing of its Portland, Maine, facility.

BIW, Maine's largest private employer, said it would seek financial aid from the state and ask the city of Bath to create a tax increment financing district that would lower the company's tax bill for 25 years.

BIW is one of two shipyards authorized by the U.S. Navy to build Aegis-type destroyers and cruisers. It recently won a contract to help build a new amphibious assault ship and is a leading bidder for a proposed assault ship.

BIW's expansion proposal calls for $200 million to be spent to expand the shipyard into the Kennebec River for a new construction area. The area would be financed and owned by a proposed state port authority and leased back to BIW.
The company said General Dynamics would invest $107 million in capital improvements over the next 10 years, including the purchase of a new drydock.
Officials said the proposal could negate the need for BIW's current drydock in Portland, but they also said they would attempt to generate enough business to keep both facilities in operation.
Portland officials have said they might not fight a closing of their city's drydock because the land used by BIW's facility might be needed for an expansion of the city's passenger ship terminal.
